#!/bin/sh

# Flux directives translated from SLURM
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 16
#FLUX: -t 01:00:00
#FLUX: -q normal256
#FLUX: -o POI16.eo%J

#
# --- Omitted SLURM options and explanations ---
#
# -J HAICprep
#   Omitted. The job name in Flux is generally set during submission (e.g.,
#   'flux submit --job-name=HAICprep ...') or via the FLUX_JOB_NAME
#   environment variable, not through a script directive.
#
# -e POI16.eo%j
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into the single output file
#   specified by the -o directive by default. This behavior matches the original request.
#

# Echo des commandes
ulimit -c 0
ulimit -s unlimited
# Nom de la machine
hostname 

. ~rodierq/DEV_57/MNH-PHYEX070-b95d84d7/conf/profile_mesonh-LXifort-R8I4-MNH-V5-6-2-ECRAD140-MPIAUTO-O2-HAIC

# 'flux run' is the native job launcher for Flux. It will automatically use the
# 16 tasks requested in the '#FLUX: -n 16' directive.

ln -sf ../01_prep_pgd/PGD.* .
ln -sf ~/SAVE/mesonh/PGD/pgd_guyane* .
ln -sf ~/SAVE/GRIB_KTEST/arome.FO.201505* .
ln -sf ~/SAVE/GRIB_KTEST/historic.20150529.00.lfi

touch pgd_guyane.02km50.04.des
touch historic.20150529.00.des

# Note: The executable command relies on an environment variable, ${XYZ}, which must
# be set in the submission environment.
time flux run PREP_REAL_CASE${XYZ}

for i in 00 06 12 18 24; do
    cp PRE_REAL1.nam_$i PRE_REAL1.nam
    time flux run PREP_REAL_CASE${XYZ}
done
cd ../
./run_all_mesonh

issues: The most significant resource-related issue is the lack of an explicit memory request. The original SLURM script also omitted this. For an MPI job running on 16 cores, this is a critical omission. The job is at high risk of being scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, leading to an out-of-memory failure, or it could be killed by the system for over-subscription.

The script is extremely non-portable. It sources a profile script from a hardcoded, user-specific path (`~rodierq/...`) and creates symlinks to files in another user-specific path (`~/SAVE/...`). This will fail for any other user.

The main executable command `time flux run PREP_REAL_CASE${XYZ}` relies on an environment variable `${XYZ}` which is not defined within the script. The job will fail unless this variable is set in the submission environment.

The script runs the main parallel application `flux run PREP_REAL_CASE${XYZ}` multiple times inside a loop. This is an inefficient way to run a workflow and may not be the intended behavior. The final `./run_all_mesonh` is a serial command that does not use the 16-task allocation and may also be a parallel launcher that needs to be adapted for Flux.

#!/bin/sh

#SBATCH -e POI16.eo%j   #
#SBATCH -t 01:00:00     # time limit
#SBATCH -p normal256

# Echo des commandes
ulimit -c 0
ulimit -s unlimited
# Nom de la machine
hostname 

. ~rodierq/DEV_57/MNH-PHYEX070-b95d84d7/conf/profile_mesonh-LXifort-R8I4-MNH-V5-6-2-ECRAD140-MPIAUTO-O2-HAIC

export MPIRUN='Mpirun -np 16'

ln -sf ../01_prep_pgd/PGD.* .
ln -sf ~/SAVE/mesonh/PGD/pgd_guyane* .
ln -sf ~/SAVE/GRIB_KTEST/arome.FO.201505* .
ln -sf ~/SAVE/GRIB_KTEST/historic.20150529.00.lfi

touch pgd_guyane.02km50.04.des
touch historic.20150529.00.des

time ${MPIRUN} PREP_REAL_CASE${XYZ}

for i in 00 06 12 18 24; do
    cp PRE_REAL1.nam_$i PRE_REAL1.nam
